article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Evening Brief
article.dek: Inactives are final for tonight's Patriots-Bears game: New England gets its right tackle back, Chicago loses a linebacker — and the line never moved all day.

items.headline: Tonight, 8:15 p.m. ET: Moses is active, Vera-Tucker to IR
paragraphs: The Patriots get their right tackle back. Morgan Moses, questionable with a foot injury, is officially active tonight — and so is every other questionable Patriot: safety Kevin Byard III, linebacker Christian Elliss, safety Craig Woodson, and cornerback Christian Gonzalez, who was added to the report Thursday with an illness.

The cost: the Patriots put guard Alijah Vera-Tucker on injured reserve with his hamstring injury, so he is out at least four games. Already ruled out: guard Ben Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis III, and backup corners Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor start at guard.

Chicago loses a defender. Linebacker T.J. Edwards, doubtful this morning, is officially out — joining running back Kyle Monangai and linebacker Jack Sanborn. The Bears elevated running back Zavier Scott and linebacker Buddy Johnson from the practice squad.
items.takeaway: Inactives are the last news of the night — everything after is price. Compare your book's line to the app's and run it through Check.

items.headline: McCarthy takes first-team reps — the app still hasn't caught up
paragraphs: J.J. McCarthy practiced with the first team Thursday ahead of Sunday's game at Houston. Head coach John Harbaugh said McCarthy 'gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can.' Jameis Winston is the backup; Jake Haener is the emergency third quarterback.

The app's evening board still lists Winston as the expected starter, so its Giants number — Houston -10.5 — is priced on the old quarterback. Do not trust the app's Giants numbers until the update lands.
One for Sunday: Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair returned to practice Thursday on a limited basis with his knee injury and is trending toward playing against the rookie starter.
items.takeaway: New quarterback news beats old model math. Let the app update, then Check the price — do not pay Winston's price for McCarthy's arm.

items.headline: Around the league: Lamar back on the field, Jacobs' first real practice
paragraphs: Lamar Jackson opened Thursday's practice in uniform with the quarterbacks — the first time since his Oct. 4 ankle injury. He's still officially limited, and the Ravens' coordinator said there's 'still a lot of work to do' for Sunday. Also in Baltimore: linebacker Tavius Robinson missed a second straight practice and safety Jaylinn Hawkins went from limited to out on Thursday.

Josh Jacobs had his first on-field practice of the season Thursday and is expected to suit up and start Sunday against Detroit. Quarterback Jordan Love was limited Thursday with a back injury — his first such listing this season — but said there's 'no chance' he misses Sunday.

Also Thursday: Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting was upheld on appeal. Buffalo is on a bye this week, so he misses the Week 8 game against the Ravens. Minor moves: the Eagles are signing guard Evan Neal; the Steelers and Buccaneers put defenders Sebastian Joseph-Day and Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve.
items.takeaway: Practice reports are signals, not verdicts. Friday's designations are the news that actually moves Sunday prices.

items.headline: Weather: clean tonight, nothing to fade
paragraphs: The National Weather Service has Soldier Field mostly clear at kickoff, around 54 degrees with an east-northeast wind near 5 mph. No precipitation, no alerts. Same clean picture as this morning.
items.takeaway: File weather under not a factor tonight. The line is the story, not the sky.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Tonight inside the app: model at 2.3, market at -3
paragraphs: The app's model prices the game at Bears by about 2.3 points; the market sits at Bears -3 with a 50.5 total. The inactive news — Moses active, Edwards out — is already inside those numbers.

That makes your price the edge. DraftKings has Chicago -3 at -110, FanDuel at -105, Pinnacle at -101. And remember what the number means: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. Small price differences are real money on a three-point spread.
items.takeaway: When the model and the market agree, the only thing left is your book's price. Tap Check, type it in, get a verdict.

items.headline: Sunday's cards: Minnesota to win, Cleveland for balance, Tampa Bay for value
paragraphs: Hit Rate is Minnesota. Colts at Vikings, Minnesota -285 on DraftKings, and the app gives them a 78.6% chance — the pick that looks most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability; the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate, and that's fine — that's its job.
Balanced is Cleveland. Browns at Titans, Cleveland -126 on FanDuel at a 71.9% model chance. A strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, a good starting point for a new bettor.
Value is Tampa Bay. Buccaneers at Panthers, Tampa Bay +3 at +100 on DraftKings — the model's +EV play. Value is always the model's +EV play.
items.takeaway: Three different jobs, three different cards. Pick the job first, then Check the price.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers
paragraphs: A 'key number' is a final margin that NFL games land on more than any other. The big ones are 3 and 7 — so many games end with a field-goal or touchdown difference.

A concrete, clearly-labeled hypothetical: say you bet a team favored by 3 and they win by exactly 3. That's a push — your stake comes back. If you had bought the same team at -2.5 instead, you'd have a win instead of a push. Half a point across a key number is worth real money.

That's why books try to move the price before they move the number. When the line sits at -3 but the price slides from -115 to -105, the book is inviting action without changing its mind about the game. Same bet, cheaper to buy.
items.takeaway: Around key numbers, the price is part of the bet — a cheaper price on the same side is the closest thing to free money this game has.

items.headline: Thursday: -3 holds, DK shades the price, Value card flips
paragraphs: Bears -3 held all day: FanDuel -105 and Pinnacle -101 on the evening board, while DraftKings shaded the Bears price from -102 this morning to -110 — same line, more expensive. Total 50.5 across all three books, unchanged.

The app's evening refresh has all of these numbers, so the board hasn't missed anything. One card changed: the Value card moved from Atlanta +2.5 to Tampa Bay +3 at even money on DraftKings. That's a recommendation replacement — the model's +EV pick changed, not the market's price.
items.takeaway: Tonight's timing note: no more news is coming before kickoff — if your book has a number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. Sunday still has one real information event left: Friday's final designations. That's the only wait in this edition.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The board refreshed this evening and refreshes again in the morning. On a one-game night, the discipline is the same as any night: only the price you can actually bet is real. Run your book's actual line and price through Check — the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and hands you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price, not anyone else's.
If Check says no bet, the evening's entertainment is free. If it says bet, you caught the right number on the right night.
items.takeaway: Check your price before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff — after that, the only thing left is watching.
